claims.text: DFT-based simulations of oxide formation can predict oxidation behavior in metallic materials at high temperature.
DFT-based simulations can be used to enhance the oxidation resistance of metallic materials.
The initial material is a crystalline titanium alloy such as Ti-6Al-4V with a clean, polished surface and minimal defects or impurities.
DFT-based simulations are applied to model oxide formation on the titanium-alloy surface.
The relevant oxidation conditions are temperatures above 500°C and an oxygen partial pressure of 1 atm.
A stable oxide layer, such as TiO2, forms on the titanium-alloy surface.
DFT-based simulations can predict the thermodynamic stability of oxide formation.
DFT-based simulations can predict kinetic barriers associated with oxide formation.
Predicted oxide stability and kinetic barriers can identify material compositions and surface treatments that improve oxidation resistance.
DFT-guided optimization will reduce the oxidation rate by 25% to 35% relative to unoptimized Ti-6Al-4V under the same conditions.
Material processing, surface preparation, and experimental conditions may affect the accuracy of the predicted oxidation outcome.
Failure to measure an oxidation rate at least 25% lower than the unoptimized baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies only the application of a simulation, whereas the outcome assumes a physically optimized material produced through simulation-guided changes; no actual composition or surface-treatment intervention is specified.
